submitted.summary: For every finite graph admitting a valid orientation, every integer between its lower and upper orientable total domination numbers is attained. This proves the interpolation conjecture, including disconnected graphs.
submitted.body:
The proof proceeds by induction on the number of edges on which two valid orientations disagree. If every disagreeing arc is the unique incoming arc at its head, a forced-head argument transfers every total dominating set from the first orientation to the target. Otherwise, a suitable arc can be reversed while retaining positive indegree; adjoining one vertex repairs total domination. Whenever the target value is strictly higher, this safe flip decreases disagreement and raises the available upper bound by at most one, yielding every intermediate integer. No connectedness assumption is needed. The proof does not assume that all valid orientations are connected by single-edge flips.

**Complete proof and verification sources:** [Interpolation of orientable total domination by safe arc reversals: a proof of the Hansen-Lai-Yue conjecture (JCMCC 1999; Anderson-Dravec-Johnston-Kuenzel Conjecture 3.1, arXiv:2311.16307)](https://mathdb.com/abs/2611.00052) · [PDF](https://mathdb.com/pdf/2611.00052v1).

The paper page includes `proof-sources.json` and `extract_sources.py`, which reconstruct the proof sources. The Lean certificate proves the stated finite-graph theorem. The paper records formalization and trust limits.
